text:
maia: quick heads-up — nightly kernel harness flagged a perf regression for candidate 'kv-opt-v2' on AArch64 (Graviton3-like). p50 +12%, p95 +22%, p99 +27% for seqlen 32-128 with small batches.
ryan_k: link to the run: https://ci.redwood/2077778888/artifacts (summary table + diffs).
maia: repro command we used: ```./kernel-bench --kernel=kv-opt-v2 --arch=aarch64 --seq=64 --batch=2 --iters=1000``` output attached in artifacts.
cheng_w: quick glance at perf: big uptick in L1d miss rate and branch-mispredicts compared to baseline kernel. flamegraph shows more time in matmul remainder path.
anya_prod: were KV-prefix caches enabled in that run? Prefix caching can change memory access patterns.
perf-bot: automated alert: regression detected in nightly-scan (job 2077778888). Delta p95=+22% (95% CI). Run tags: arch=aarch64, quant=4bit, cache=enabled.
sam_dev: I can reproduce locally on our aarch64 perf box. Running `perf record -g` now, will share folded stack.
ryan_k: my suspicion: autotuner's kernel-picker score function underweights architecture-specific penalty for Scalar remainder path. It prefers kv-opt-v2 for seq<128, but the cost model doesn't capture L1 thrash on AArch64.
cheng_w: quick snippet from kernel selector: ```if (seq <= 64 && score(kernel_opt) < score(baseline)) choose kernel_opt;``` — we need to include arch_weight in score.
maia: mitigation idea: rollback canary for kv-opt-v2 on aarch64 and pin dedicated customers to baseline until fix. Can we add a rollout rule?
anya_prod: +1. I can apply a temporary rollout policy: canary=false for arch=aarch64. Will need a small console change.
sam_dev: opening a PR to gate kv-opt-v2 for aarch64 in the nightly CI and add a test that fails if p95 regresses >10%: https://git.redwood/pr/5234
ci-bot: created ticket INF-2342 (kernel autotune regression) and linked PR 5234.
maia: owners: sam_dev (repro + PR), cheng_w (kernel selector + perf profile), ryan_k (autotuner scoring), anya_prod (rollout rule). Perf-bot please re-run targeted microbench with perf sampling after PR lands.
perf-bot: scheduled targeted re-run in 2 hours, will post results in this thread.
ryan_k: plausible root cause: quantized SIMD path on aarch64 has scalar tail that hits a different codegen than x86; for small batches overhead dominates. Short-term patch: prefer baseline kernel for seq<=128 on AArch64 or adjust autotuner cost to add +20% overhead for remainder handling.
cheng_w: if we add arch-aware penalty, let's also extend autotuner tests: run across seq buckets [16,32,64,128,256] and batch buckets [1,2,4,8] across all supported arches.
maia: good call. also add a metric to track L1d miss delta automatically in CI so we can catch similar regressions earlier.
sam_dev: posted repro logs and perf script in artifacts at https://ci.redwood/2077778888/perf. I included a small script to reproduce: ```#!/bin/bash
./kernel-bench --kernel=kv-opt-v2 --arch=aarch64 --seq=64 --batch=2 --iters=200 | tee kv-opt-v2.seq64.b2.log
perf record -o kv-opt-v2.seq64.b2.perf -g -- ./kernel-bench --kernel=kv-opt-v2 --arch=aarch64 --seq=64 --batch=2 --iters=200
perf script -i kv-opt-v2.seq64.b2.perf > folded.stacks
# generate flamegraph (local)
```
anya_prod: once PR merges, I'll trigger a canary rollout for dedicated customers to confirm OK before full unblock.
maia: thanks everyone. next steps: sam -> PR + repro artifacts, cheng -> propose autotuner score change, ryan -> draft small fallback patch, anya -> apply temporary rollout and monitor. Perf-bot re-run expected in ~2h.
perf-bot: re-run complete: p95 delta down to +3% after forcing baseline kernel on aarch64 in canary. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/2077778888/re-run.
maia: great, that confirms selector decision is the culprit. We'll keep baseline as default for aarch64 until autotuner score is updated and autotune sweep passes.
ryan_k: I'll start a sweep job with adjusted arch_weight and post results here.
cheng_w: I'll add a unit test for the selector to assert arch_weight presence in score vector.
sam_dev: closing loop: I'll add the CI guard so future merges require perf non-regression for the seq/batch buckets.
maia: closing — filing a short postmortem follow-up doc and linking INF-2342. Thanks all :thumbsup:
